detail.longDescription: Hey HN, I've been working on rmux, an open source terminal workspace built in Rust using GPUI and Ghostty's terminal engine. The main focus has been performance. I wanted something that could handle multiple projects, shells and coding agents without becoming a resource hog or feeling sluggish as more panes are opened, which has been a frustration I've had with some other terminals. I also have a sweet setup for it to be my standard external terminal for VS Code where I can switch back and forth between the same workspace in VS Code and rmux with a single shortcut. I share the details of how that's done on the VS Code page on the website. It supports named workspaces, tabs, split panes, keyboard shortcuts and a command palette. Nothing particularly revolutionary in terms of features, but the goal is to make the experience as responsive and lightweight as possible. Of course the site has a WASM demo - because it's in Rust and that's what the cool people do. Would be interested to hear what people think, particularly around performance and the overall UX. Source is on GitHub, linked from the website.
